findings.title: New non-default order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: CryptoProvider is a public service-loader interface. Adding `int order()` as a non-default method breaks source and binary compatibility for any external or extension implementation compiled against the previous interface. Such implementations will fail to compile, or fail at runtime with an AbstractMethodError/NoSuchMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts discovered providers. A default method would preserve compatibility.

findings.title: Multiple CryptoProviders are now silently resolved, including equal-order ties
findings.body: detectProvider no longer fails when multiple CryptoProvider implementations are present; it instantiates all of them, sorts by order, and selects the first. Default, Elytron, and FIPS providers all return order 200, so if two are accidentally present the chosen provider depends on ServiceLoader/classpath ordering. This can silently select the wrong crypto implementation. It also means ignored providers are still constructed; providers such as FIPS1402Provider register JCA providers and modify global security properties in their constructors, so an ignored provider can still affect the JVM.

findings.title: ECDSA conversion does not validate raw signature length
findings.body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER assumes the raw concatenated ECDSA signature has exactly `signLength` bytes and immediately copies `signLength / 2` bytes from it. If a malformed signature is shorter than expected, this throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException; if it is longer, extra bytes are silently ignored. The method should validate `signature.length == signLength` and reject invalid input with IOException.

findings.title: ECDSA integer-to-bytes conversion silently truncates or mishandles invalid values
findings.body: integerToBytes copies only the last `qLength` bytes when a parsed BigInteger encoding is longer than expected, silently truncating an oversized r/s value. It also does not reject negative ASN.1 INTEGER values; converting a negative BigInteger with zero padding produces an incorrect unsigned fixed-length octet string. Malformed ECDSA signature components should be rejected rather than transformed.

findings.title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding is not handled
findings.body: readLength can return -1 for indefinite-length encoding, but readInteger passes that value directly to read(int), causing NegativeArraySizeException. readSequence also treats -1 as an empty sequence instead of rejecting the input. DER-encoded ECDSA signatures should not use indefinite length; the decoder should throw IOException when it encounters this case.

findings.title: Sequence parsing is not strict about lengths or trailing data
findings.body: readSequence subtracts each child TLV length from the declared sequence length but does not verify that a child length fits within the remaining sequence bytes, so malformed overlong children can make the remaining length negative without error. It also does not verify that all input bytes were consumed after parsing the sequence, allowing trailing garbage after the DER sequence. Cryptographic signature parsing should reject such malformed DER input.

findings.title: ECDSA tests do not use curve-specific keys or verify signatures
findings.body: The test generates one default EC key pair and uses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512, then only asserts that DER-to-concatenated and concatenated-to-DER conversions round-trip. It does not verify that the converted signature is valid for the expected curve/key size, nor does it use P-256, P-384, and P-521 keys or known test vectors. This can miss incorrect handling of curve-specific signature lengths or malformed signatures.
